claims.text: An ultra-thin Al2O3 interlayer between zirconium alloy and elemental Cr will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The Al2O3 interlayer will improve Cr-coating durability under both subcritical-water and high-temperature steam conditions.
The proposed Al2O3 interlayer is nanometer-scale and conformal.
The Al2O3 barrier is chemically inert in the proposed system.
The ultra-thin Al2O3 barrier remains stable over the stated operating-temperature range.
Al2O3 acts as a physical diffusion barrier to chromium and zirconium atoms.
Limiting Cr and Zr transport will prevent formation of deleterious intermetallic compounds.
At moderate temperatures, the Al2O3 interlayer will preserve the oxidation resistance supplied by the Cr coating.
At high temperatures, mitigation of interdiffusion will maintain coating integrity and reduce interdiffusion-driven failure.
Relative to directly Cr-coated cladding, the modified system will have lower oxidation rates.
Relative to directly Cr-coated cladding, the modified system will exhibit less interfacial element transport.
Relative to directly Cr-coated cladding, the modified system will exhibit better mechanical coating integrity.
A directly deposited elemental Cr coating is prone to premature failure caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed intervention is applicable from approximately 300°C in subcritical water to approximately 1000°C in high-temperature steam.
The proposed intervention is applicable over exposures ranging from accident-relevant hours to extended reactor-operational periods.
The intervention's benefit will depend on Al2O3-layer uniformity and stability under prolonged and cyclic thermal stresses.

contradictions.description: The structural-mediator field categorically describes the ultra-thin Al2O3 layer as stable at operating temperatures, while the uncertainty field states that its stability under prolonged and cyclic thermal stress is uncertain.
